text.p: Swedish phone equipment company LM Ericsson rose on Friday to highlight the market in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
European ADRs were mostly stronger in quiet trade. They were helped by a Wall Street rally stemming from U.S. job and wage data that eased worries about an interest rate rise.
"All the activity appears to be in the domestic market," a trader said. "The markets are not racing away, but we're seeing some confidence."

Ericsson rose 1-5/16 to 35-1/8 on heavy volume boosted by general strength in the telecommunications equipment sector and by news that Sweden's unemployment rate had remained unchanged in February. Ericsson and the United States' Motorola Inc also won a contract this week for a mobile phone network in India.
Fellow Nordic telecommunications equipment maker Nokia Group of Finland also was up, rising 1-3/8 to 62-5/8.
British pharmaceutical company Glaxo Wellcome Plc rose 1-1/8 to 34-7/8 in heavy trade, buoyed by upbeat press comment on the company's 1996 results.
Italian state telephone holding Stet rose 1-3/4 to 47 in moderate trade after a hard-left party softened its opposition to the company's privatization.
Among Latin American ADRs, Telefonos de Mexico rose 5/8 to 39-5/8.
Advancers led decliners by 256 to 204 among 806 ADRs. Volume was 28 million shares.
